headline: California Holds Data Centers Accountable for Infrastructure Costs
meta_description: Governor Newsom signs seven laws requiring data centers to pay their fair share of electricity and water infrastructure costs while disclosing environmental im…
summary_short: California just took a major step to ensure data centers pay their fair share. Seven new laws will require disclosure of water use and environmental review.
body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has signed seven laws designed to make data centers shoulder their fair share of electricity and water infrastructure costs. The legislation also requires data centers to disclose their water use and undergo environmental review—measures that will protect the state's resources and communities.

Data centers consume enormous amounts of water and electricity, yet their environmental costs have often been absorbed by local communities and taxpayers. These new laws represent a significant shift toward accountability in an industry that powers much of the digital economy. By requiring transparency about water consumption and formal environmental assessments, California is setting a model for how states can balance technological growth with environmental protection.
quick_facts: Governor Gavin Newsom signed seven new data center laws
Laws require data centers to pay for electricity and water infrastructure
Data centers must now disclose water use to the public
Environmental review now required before data center operations
California protects local communities from hidden environmental costs
